extracted.intended_audience: journalists and news organizations submitting work for the George Polk Awards (including Schanberg Prize applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluative criteria for works submitted to the George Polk Awards (and the Sydney H. Schanberg Prize) — focused on recognizing outstanding journalism across media, with special rules for long-form investigative entries. Useful for journalists and newsrooms preparing award submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall focus: intrepid, bold, and influential reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: This prestigious honor focuses on the intrepid, bold, and influential work of the reporters themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The George Polk Awards place a premium on investigative work that is original, resourceful, and thought-provoking; the program recognizes reporting across all media and highlights the reporters' work rather than simply the outlet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative reporting: originality, digging, resourcefulness, and impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges place a premium on investigative work that is original, requires digging and resourcefulness, and brings results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should demonstrate original reporting (not merely synthesis), show evidence of thorough investigation and resourcefulness in reporting, and where possible document tangible outcomes or effects (i.e., 'brings results').

rubrics_metrics.name: Media/format eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Winners are chosen from newspapers, magazines, television, radio and online news organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The awards recognize reporting across all media formats — print, broadcast, and digital — and are not limited to a single medium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schanberg Prize: long-form investigative/enterprise journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Awarded annually for exceptional long-form investigative or enterprise journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articles must be at least 5,000 words in length and represent highly distinguished, deep coverage of specified topics (see next metric). The prize honors long-form, deeply reported pieces and is funded by Jane Freiman Schanberg.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schanberg Prize topical eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible long-form pieces must cover one or more of: armed conflicts; local, state or Federal government corruption; military injustice; war crimes, genocide or sedition; or authoritarian government abuses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions for the Sydney H. Schanberg Prize must be highly distinguished, deep coverage of these serious subject areas; topic scope is explicitly limited to these categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award categories / types of recognized work
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of categories highlighted on the page include: Intrepid Reporting, Powerful Photography, In-depth Articles, Exposés, Investigations, Significant Enterprise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These category labels indicate the range of journalistic work the Polk Awards recognize — from photography to exposés to enterprise reporting — and can guide applicants on how their work maps to award types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on the reporter (laureate-centric recognition)
rubrics_metrics.description: The awards emphasize and honor 'the reporters themselves' rather than primarily the organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing submissions, highlight the reporting work and the reporter's contribution, courage, and craft, as the prize historically recognizes individual journalistic achievement.
